newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev firms on support from bank, Finmin.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev firms on support from bank, Finmin.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 1,560-1,590 per dollar, up from the morning's 1,600-1,630 as a large bank supported it and the Finance Minister said pressure on lev was highly speculative, dealers said.

"A large state-owned commercial bank began offering relatively large dollar volumes in the afternoon and pressure on the lev subsided. The lev closed some 40 (levs per dollar) stronger," one dealer said.

Some banks and final clients withdrew from the market around midday either because they have purchased the small dollar volumes they needed or because they considered the levels near 1,630 as too low for the lev.
The lev closed at 1,535-1,545 on Friday.
Trade was range-bound between 1,560-1,590 levs per dollar in the afternoon as market calm was restored by the Finance Minister's comments.
"I see no fundamental reasons for a further slide because today's fall was due to speculation that the dollar will sharply rise after the poll," Svetoslav Gavriiski told reporters.
It was unjustified talk that the interim cabinet has stabilised the lev between 1,500-1,600 since early March through administrative measures, said Gavriiski.
"Bulgaria has secured enough foreign funding to service its foreign debt payments this year through its reserves and the budget," Gavriiski said.
The interim cabinet has won pledges of some $1.2 billion of funding from international lenders, including a $657 million funding package from the International Monetary Fund.
The pro-reform Union of Democratic Forces won a big parliamantary majority in Saturday's elections and was expected to carry on with painful economic reforms launched by the interim cabinet.
The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said on Monday its foreign exchange reserves rose to $1.09 billion on April 21 from $554.3 million on March 31.
This compared with $656 million Bulgaria has to pay on its foreign debt in the remaining three quarters, BNB figures showed.
